questiontext.text:
The red shape is shown on the coordinate plane, together with the dashed mirror line \( y = {@lineexpr@} \).

Reflect the shape in the line \( y = {@lineexpr@} \) by dragging the blue vertices to their image positions.

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

Reflect each vertex straight across the dashed line \( y = {@lineexpr@} \): its image sits the same perpendicular distance away, on the other side. Join the images in the same order to get the green shape.

The thin lines join each vertex to its image. Each one meets the mirror line at a right angle, and the line cuts it exactly in half.

' + ' + c : ' - ' + (-c)))], { fontSize: 12, color: '#888888', fixed: true, anchorX: 'left' }); function drawShape(coords, col, fillop) { var pts = coords.map(function (p) { return board.create('point', p, { visible: false, fixed: true }); }); board.create('polygon', pts, { fillColor: col, fillOpacity: fillop, borders: { strokeColor: col, strokeWidth: 3 }, fixed: true, vertices: { visible: false } }); } var origPts = {#base_shape#}; var reflPts = {#reflected_shape#}; drawShape(origPts, '#d62728', 0.15); // original (red) drawShape(reflPts, '#2ca02c', 0.30); // reflected (green) // Perpendicular construction lines: each vertex joined to its image for (var i = 0; i < origPts.length; i++) { board.create('segment', [origPts[i], reflPts[i]], { strokeColor: '#555555', strokeWidth: 1, dash: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false }); board.create('point', [ (origPts[i][0] + reflPts[i][0]) / 2, (origPts[i][1] + reflPts[i][1]) / 2 ], { size: 1, color: '#555555', fixed: true, withLabel: false, highlight: false }); } board.renderer.svgRoot.style.pointerEvents = "none"; [[/jsxgraph]]

truefeedback.text: You have slid the shape to a new position, but it is still facing the same way. A reflection flips the shape over the dashed line, like a mirror image, so it ends up back-to-front. Picture folding the paper along the line: the shape should land on the far side, turned over.

You have reflected in the y-axis (the vertical line), not the dashed 45° line. Use the dashed line as your mirror: each vertex should end up the same perpendicular distance from that line, straight across it on the other side.

You have reflected in the x-axis (the horizontal line), not the dashed 45° line. Reflect in the dashed line instead: look straight across it at right angles, and place each vertex the same distance beyond it.

node.description: Reflected in y = x (line through the origin)?

truefeedback.text: Close! You have reflected in the line \(y = x\) through the origin, but the mirror line here is the parallel line \(y = {@lineexpr@}\). Measure the perpendicular distance to the dashed line, which is shifted to one side of \(y = x\).

falsefeedback.text: Not yet. Picture folding the plane along the dashed line so the two sides meet. Each vertex should map to the point straight across the line, the same perpendicular distance away on the opposite side.
